title: The Three Billy Goats Gruff
place: A bridge below a green mountain meadow
sourceAuthor: Peter Christen Asbjørnsen and Jørgen Moe; translated by George Webbe Dasent
note: A new adaptation of “The Three Billy-Goats Gruff,” preserving the familiar trip-trap pattern and softening the source’s violent ending.

rights.basis: Source edition published in the nineteenth century and identified as public domain by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: Three goats cross a wooden bridge while a troll watches below.
scenes: Three goats named Gruff longed for the sweet grass on the mountain. To reach it, they had to cross a bridge where a hungry troll lived.
Trip-trap went the littlest goat. The troll roared, but the goat said, “Wait for my brother—he is much bigger.” The troll let him pass.
Trip-trap, trip-trap went the middle goat. He gave the same warning, and the greedy troll waited again.
TRAMP-TRAMP came the biggest Gruff. The troll leaped onto the bridge. Big Gruff lowered his strong horns and charged.
The troll tumbled into the rushing river and floated far downstream. All three goats climbed safely to the meadow, where there was enough green grass for everyone.
